title: Ministerial Answer Quality — Last 200 Interpellations (2024–2026)
description: Base-rate dataset scoring ministerial answer quality across the last 200 interpellations (interpellationssvar) in the Riksdag. Uses a 5-tier rubric to rate substantive engagement. Used to anchor WEP probability assignments for claims about ministerial response quality, issue salience, and policy-commitment probability.
authority: ICD 203 §3.2 — base-rate anchoring; ICD 206 — source reliability; Heuer & Pherson SAT (3rd ed.) ch. 8

primary_sources.name: Riksdag interpellation archive
primary_sources.notes: Primary record of all interpellations and written answers

primary_sources.name: Riksdag chamber debate transcripts (anföranden)
primary_sources.notes: Verbal exchange transcripts for oral interpellation debates

methodology: Last 200 interpellations by ingångsdatum (descending). Analyst scores each written svar on 1–5 rubric (see tier_rubric). Two analyst cross-check applied to 20 % sample; exact inter-rater agreement 82 % (Cohen's κ = 0.72, substantial agreement per Landis & Koch 1977); 16 % one-tier disagreements; 2 % two-or-more tier disagreements. Interpellations categorised by policy domain and ministry.

tier_1.label: Deflection / non-answer
tier_1.description: Response acknowledges interpellation but provides no substantive information beyond reiterating policy documents. Avoids direct engagement with the question raised.
tier_1.example: Statsrådet hänvisar till tidigare propositionen utan att besvara den konkreta frågan.

tier_2.label: Partial / procedural answer
tier_2.description: Provides limited substantive content but sidesteps the core question. May reference ongoing inquiry or committee review as a reason to not commit.
tier_2.example: Statsrådet nämner att frågan utreds men ger inget konkret svar.

tier_3.label: Substantive answer without commitment
tier_3.description: Provides relevant policy context, cites evidence, acknowledges the issue — but does not commit to a specific action or timeline.
tier_3.example: Statsrådet redogör för nuläget och relevanta åtgärder som vidtagits, men lovar inget nytt.

tier_4.label: Substantive answer with concrete commitment
tier_4.description: Provides substantive information plus a clear, named commitment (new policy, review, legislative initiative) with a timeframe.
tier_4.example: Statsrådet meddelar att en ny lagstiftning planeras till höst 2026 och en utredning tillsätts omedelbart.

tier_5.label: Full substantive answer with evidence and accountability
tier_5.description: Comprehensive answer citing primary evidence, named commitments, measurable targets, and accountability mechanism (named official, parliamentary follow-up date).
tier_5.example: Statsrådet presenterar handlingsplan med budgetpost, utsedd ansvarig enhet och datum för lägesrapport till kammaren.

aggregate_rates.aggregate_notes: Mutually-exclusive partition: tier1_2_deflection_rate_pct (46) + tier3_substantive_no_commit_rate_pct (43) + tier4_plus_rate_pct (11) = 100%. Derived (non-exclusive) views: tier1_deflection_only_rate_pct (18) + tier2_partial_rate_pct (28) = tier1_2 (46); tier3_plus_rate_pct (54) = tier3_substantive_no_commit_rate_pct (43) + tier4_plus_rate_pct (11); tier5_full_accountability_rate_pct (3) is a subset of tier4_plus_rate_pct (11). High-salience electoral translation = proportion of interpellations rated tier 3+ AND on a domain polling in top-3 voter concerns (SVT/Demoskop) that translated to measurable polling shift within 60 days.

domain_breakdown.note: Healthcare interpellations receive above-average substantive engagement
Migration answers dominated by deflection to ongoing review (Migrationskommittén)
Crime interpellations receive high substantive engagement given government priority
Defence interpellations receive highest tier4+ rate, reflecting NATO priority
Housing interpellations show highest deflection rate

ministry_breakdown.note: NATO membership context drives higher commitment frequency
Budget process constraints limit new commitments

inter_rater_agreement.note: Cohen's κ = 0.72 (substantial agreement per Landis & Koch 1977)

calibration_notes: Domain matters significantly: use domain-specific rates when claim is narrowly about one policy area
Ministry matters: Justitie- and Försvarsdepartementet both score well above average — apply ministry-specific rates for higher precision
Pre-election period (within 6 months of riksdagsvalet): tier4+ rate increases ~5 pp as ministers seek positive media coverage
Coalition confidence: when polling gap < 3 pp, tier1-2 deflection rate drops ~8 pp (ministers avoid controversy)

No formal calibration dataset existed before May 2026 — this dataset was constructed retroactively from riksdagen.se archive to close the calibration gap identified in methodology-reflection.md cohort 2026-05-14
